title: Cohomology bound from an affine atlas of a separated algebraic space
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y$ a quasi-compact separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Quasi-compact means that every open cover of $|Y|$ has a finite subcover, and separated means that the absolute representable diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $v:V\to Y$ be a representable surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $d\geq1$ be an integer such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, the geometric fibre $V\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has at most $d$ points [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, def-weil-geometric-point]. Then for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $N$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and every integer $q\geq d$,
$$H^q(Y_{\mathrm{et}},N_{ab})=0.$$
Here $N_{ab}$ is the underlying abelian sheaf and cohomology is the right derived functor of abelian-sheaf global sections [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The bound uses only the atlas and its fibre bound, with no dimension, Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, using a bound on geometric fibre cardinalities (equivalently the degrees for etale geometric fibres), as in the proof by the alternating spectral sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to the structural map $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. This preserves the atlas, its sheaf fibre products, small etale ringed sites and therefore the module and its abelian-sheaf cohomology. Thus we may work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, retaining the assumed absolute separatedness of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: For $r\geq1$ put $T_r=V^{\times_Yr}$. These are affine etale charts of $Y$, by induction: $T_1=V$ and [lem-trf-space-separated-affine-chart-overlap], applied to the separated map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and the affine etale charts $T_r,V$, says that $T_{r+1}$ is affine and its projections are etale. In particular $T_2$ is affine. The diagonal $V\to T_2$ is a pairwise equality locus and is open and closed by [lem-sfb-etale-atlas-distinct-tuple-geometry]. Its scheme structure is the induced open-subscheme structure; a clopen open immersion is a closed immersion, since the sheaf map is identity on that open and has zero target on its open complement. Thus $v$ is separated, as required by the spectral-sequence lemma.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-alternating-sign-cohomology-spectral] to $v$ and $A=N_{ab}$. Write $W_p\subset T_{p+1}$ for the complement of all pairwise equality loci, $G_p=\mathfrak S_{p+1}$, $Q_p=W_p/G_p$, $g_p:Q_p\to Y$, and $L_p$ for its sign local system. It supplies the first-quadrant sequence $E_1^{p,b}=H^b((Q_p)_{\mathrm{et}},g_p^{-1}N_{ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_p)\Rightarrow H^{p+b}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},N_{ab})$, including stabilization and the finite abutment filtration. The $G_p$-action is free on all scheme tests, the quotient is the fppf orbit sheaf, and $L_p$ is trivialized by the covering $W_p\to Q_p$.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: Each $W_p$ is open and closed in the affine $T_{p+1}$. Indeed the finitely many equality loci are clopen by [lem-sfb-etale-atlas-distinct-tuple-geometry]. Its open inclusion is a closed immersion: on the decomposition into it and its open complement the structure-sheaf map is respectively the identity and the map to zero. By the affine-open characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion], a closed subscheme of the affine $T_{p+1}$ is affine. This also covers $p=0$, where no diagonal is removed.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: Fix $p$ and put $W_p=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The action relation $R=\coprod_{g\in G_p}W_p\rightrightarrows W_p$ is affine: it is $\operatorname{Spec}\prod_g B$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](4). Each projection is finite locally free by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum], since $\prod_g B$ has the finite basis indexed by $G_p$ over $B$; for the action projection, conjugate by $(g,w)\mapsto(g,gw)$. Freeness from step 3 makes $R$ an equivalence relation on every scheme test. Apply [lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient]: the fppf orbit sheaf is represented by the affine spectrum of the equalizer ring. Hence the already specified $Q_p$ is an affine scheme. This argument never divides by $|G_p|$.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: Set $M_p=g_p^*N\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_p$, with $\mathcal O_{Q_p}$ acting on the first factor. Because $g_p$ is etale, its pullback on the small etale site is restriction [def-trf-algebraic-space]; hence $(g_p^*N)_{ab}=g_p^{-1}N_{ab}$. By the local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], restriction of $N$ has local presentations by sums of the structure sheaf. Refine each presentation cover by a cover trivializing $L_p$ supplied in step 3. There $L_p\simeq\underline{\mathbf Z}$, so $M_p\simeq g_p^*N$ and has exactly the same presentation. Those covers exhibit $M_p$ as quasi-coherent by that definition. Its underlying abelian sheaf is the coefficient in $E_1^{p,b}$. This proves the twist assertion directly, without an exactness claim about taking sign invariants.

source.place: Tag 072A, lemma-quasi-coherent-twist, proof by etale-local trivialization; Tag 0727, lemma-twist.

proof.text: For each $p$, use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] on the affine scheme $Q_p$: the quasi-coherent module $M_p$ is isomorphic to $F_{p,\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_p$. Therefore [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^b((Q_p)_{\mathrm{et}},(M_p)_{ab})=0$ for every $b>0$. Consequently $E_1^{p,b}=0$ in every positive row. These groups are on $Q_p$, not on $W_p$; the latter notation in the last lines of the printed proof of 072B is a typographical slip.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: If $p\geq d$, the geometric-fibre tuple description of [lem-sfb-etale-atlas-distinct-tuple-geometry] makes $W_p$ empty. Explicitly, an etale scheme over an algebraically closed field is a disjoint union of copies of its spectrum: apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] and the definition of algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Thus the at-most-$d$ points in the assumed geometric fibre give at most $d$ possible entries for a distinct tuple, while $p+1>d$. If $W_p$ had a point, its canonical residue-field point [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], followed by an algebraic closure, would produce just such a forbidden tuple over a geometric point of $Y$. Hence $W_p=\varnothing$, and its surjective quotient $Q_p$ is empty. A sheaf of abelian groups on the empty scheme has zero sections, since the empty covering is a covering. In particular $E_1^{p,0}=0$ for $p\geq d$.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

proof.text: For $q\geq d$, every first-page term of total degree $q$ vanishes: a term with second index positive vanishes by step 7, and the remaining term has first index $q\geq d$ and vanishes by step 8. A zero entry stays zero on subsequent pages, as the next entry is the kernel of its outgoing differential modulo the image of its incoming differential. Thus each $E_\infty^{p,q-p}$ is zero. In the finite filtration supplied by [lem-sfb-space-alternating-sign-cohomology-spectral], all successive quotients vanish; starting with $F^{q+1}=0$ and inducting backwards gives $H^q(Y_{\mathrm{et}},N_{ab})=0$. The case $Y=\varnothing$ is included by the same argument.

source.place: Tag 072B, proposition-vanishing, proof; with Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence.

No new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit, so nothing is superseded. There is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. I read Stacks 072B/0728/0727/072A in full against the 9 steps. Step 1: base change to Z (clauses 1 and 3 keep the fibres, sites and structure sheaf; the separatedness is absolute). Step 2: T_r affine by induction with 03M9 applied over Spec Z, and v separated because the diagonal is the clopen equality locus of the tuple node. Step 3: the spectral node, used only for what its statement says. Step 4: W_p is a clopen subscheme of an affine, hence affine. Step 5: R=Spec ∏_g B has finite free projections, and j is injective because the action is free (gw=g'w forces w into an equality locus off W_p); 03BM then gives Q_p=Spec C. The presheaf U(H)/R(H) and the orbit presheaf have the same fppf sheafification; this is elementary and not a fault. Step 6: twist quasi-coherent by local presentations (072A). Step 7: 03DX essential surjectivity plus affine étale acyclicity, so the rows b>0 vanish; this is on Q_p, not W_p, which correctly fixes the slip in the printed 072B. Step 8: an étale fibre over an algebraically closed field is a disjoint union of copies of Spec Ω, so there are no distinct (p+1)-tuples when p+1>d and W_p=Q_p=∅. Step 9: the finite filtration gives the vanishing. Edge cases checked: Y empty, d=1, p=0, characteristic 2, non-noetherian. Duplicates: only the 072C parent cites this item; no other node states 072B.
